name: Arctic Open
stakes: Coming off the demanding Asian Games, the Arctic Open is a critical opportunity for India's shuttlers to regroup, earn valuable Super 500 points, and build momentum for the remainder of the season.
summary:
India's badminton contingent heads to the Arctic Open after a mixed bag at the Asian Games. The demanding schedule in Nagoya has clearly taken a toll on some, notably PV Sindhu, who voiced concerns about playing three matches in 18 hours before her quarterfinal exit. This Super 500 event offers a chance to reset and build momentum.

Men's doubles pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, fresh off a men's team bronze at the Asian Games, will be looking to make a deep run. Lakshya Sen, who had an early exit in Nagoya, will be keen to find his rhythm. Youngsters like Ayush Shetty and Malvika Bansod continue to gain valuable experience on the international circuit.

The women's doubles pair of Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, along with mixed doubles duo Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto, both reached the quarterfinals at the Asian Games. Their performances in Finland will be crucial for their continued ascent in the world rankings. HS Prannoy, also part of the bronze-winning men's team, will aim for a strong individual showing.
